summary.headline: UltraTech Q4 FY26: consolidated volume about 44 Mt, EBITDA of INR1,253/t, and a INR240/share FY26 dividend, with India Cements brand migration completed.
summary.overview: The call was the UltraTech Q4 FY26 earnings call, transcript filed by India Cements Ltd as a subsidiary disclosure. UltraTech crossed 200 Mt India capacity and committed to 242.5 Mt by FY28. Q4 realisations rose about 2.5% on grey cement pricing, with consolidated EBITDA per tonne at INR1,253 (INR1,296 excluding acquired assets). Management flagged West Asia-linked cost pressure, mainly bags (about INR90 crore hit in March) and a mark-to-market forex loss (about INR120-130 crore), and said price hikes taken in April offset it. The Board recommended a INR240/share dividend for FY26, and India Cements' 100% brand migration to UltraTech was completed at end-March 2026.

financial_highlights.change: Q4 FY25 excl. acquired assets was INR1,225/t; excl. acquired assets Q4 FY26 INR1,296/t
UltraTech brand volume up 19% YoY as stated
first profit after a long time, as stated
as stated by CFO in closing remarks
up from INR333/t in Q2 and INR305/t in Q3
dividend payout 37% of profit last year as stated

segments.name: India (UltraTech India, ~196 Mt capacity)
segments.commentary: Average utilisation above 80% and about 90% per the CFO; trade mix around 66-67%. Ex-West Asia aberrations, India EBITDA was about INR1,240/t per management.

segments.name: UAE / overseas (~5 Mt)
segments.commentary: Utilisation fell from 100% pre-conflict to about 80%, now recovering. Bulk-only, so no bag cost. Q4 EBITDA INR278 crore.

segments.name: India Cements (acquired)
segments.commentary: Q4 EBITDA INR497/t, with INR200/t of underlying margin sitting in UltraTech's books under the tolling arrangement, giving about INR670/t on a combined basis. Target above INR1,000/t by FY28. Q4 volume 3.12 Mt, of which 0.39 Mt non-UltraTech brand.

segments.name: Kesoram (acquired)
segments.commentary: Already operating at more than INR1,000/t EBITDA in Q4 per management. Brand migration fully complete.

segments.name: Cable and wire
segments.commentary: About INR800 crore of an INR1,800 crore capex spent; management expects launch around Q3 FY27 (first month of Q3).

guidance_outlook: Sustainable volume growth of 7-8% per annum; double-digit volume growth targeted for FY27 (industry 6.5% for FY26 as cited by management).
Capacity to reach 242.5 Mt in phases by FY28 with 37 Mt of further additions committed; growth beyond 240 Mt being planned.
Annual capex of INR8,000-10,000 crore from internal accruals for the foreseeable future; leverage to stay below 1x.
Cost efficiency programme: about INR185/t delivered; target above INR300/t, now expected to be exceeded by FY28.
Clinker factor (clinker-to-cement ratio) target 1.54x by FY28, from 1.48x currently; the company will remain fully clinker-backed.
Green power: about 43% of power from green sources; target about 85% by end FY30.

Price hikes taken in April 2026 management views as sufficient to offset bag cost increase (about INR6/bag) and sustain profitability; diesel and June-quarter fuel (about INR1.77-1.8/kcal) not fully factored in.
capex_capacity: Capacity at 200 Mt in India; 37 Mt more committed in a phased manner, taking capacity above 242.5 Mt by FY28.
India Cements: INR1,592 crore committed for efficiency improvement, plus INR400 crore for capacity expansion; Kesoram cost-improvement capex of INR400-500 crore.
Acquired ICL and Kesoram assets together are about 13% of consolidated capacity.
No thermal capacity to be added; the mix shifts to WHRS and renewables. Lead distance 367 km; new Lucknow bulk terminal.
demand_pricing: Grey cement prices rose about 2.5% in most geographies in Q4, helped by trade mix and premiumisation; April 2026 cement price increases were taken.
Industry volume growth in the March quarter estimated at 6-7%; FY26 industry growth estimated at 6.5%.
Trade/non-trade mix about 65-68%; rural demand described as steady.
Bag prices rose from about INR9 to INR15 a bag during March, and about INR13-14 by late April. Bag supply was described as expensive but not a constraint.
Management said price hikes were 'here to stay' given cost inflation across the industry.

qa_highlights.question: Is a high payout ratio sustainable given the balance sheet and capex funded from internal accruals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it depends on performance and the Board; FY26 dividend of INR240/share is described as the highest level, with a possible repeat next year but no commitment.

qa_highlights.question: How much West Asia cost impact is in Q4 and how should June quarter look?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental bag cost in Q4 was about INR90 crore, which cannot be annualised. Power and fuel are not expected to be a large issue in June; a mark-to-market forex hit of about INR120-130 crore is in EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: How much of India Cements' INR1,000/t target comes from cost versus realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost programmes and price increases are both contributors. INR200/t of EBITDA sits in UltraTech's books; combined EBITDA is about INR670/t already, with the target including both books.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for the India Cements merger?
qa_highlights.answer: Legacy legal cases inherited with India Cements have to be closed first; management wants no risk to UltraTech before the next phase of integration.

qa_highlights.question: Is the UltraTech balance sheet ring-fenced from the group's RCB exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said not a penny has moved from the UltraTech balance sheet for other purposes, and it is committed to keeping it ring-fenced.

qa_highlights.question: Why is cement lagging other building materials on price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the lag mainly to industry fragmentation, and said price increases typically come in Q1 of the financial year.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict: sustained high pet coke (about $160/t cited by an analyst), oil near $100/bbl and diesel pass-through, which management says is not yet factored in.
Bag cost volatility and whether the April price hikes hold through monsoon (July-September).
Forex: $950 million of hedged foreign currency borrowings marked at INR94.85/$ at 31 March; the rupee moved to about INR94.2 by late April, so a mark-to-market effect can reverse.
Whether India Cements' remaining legal cases close, allowing the next integration phase.
Whether the INR200/t of India Cements EBITDA in UltraTech's books comes through and the INR300/t efficiency programme is delivered.
Sustainability of the dividend payout beyond the special FY26 payout, and the RMC (ready-mix concrete) growth plan (no monetisation planned).
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on capacity, integration and dividend, but guarded and deflecting on West Asia cost trajectory, diesel, forward pricing and the India Cements merger timeline. Several answers were framed as 'we will wait and watch'.
key_quotes: UltraTech crossed 200 million tons of cement production capacity in India, a first for any company in a single country outside of China.
We said we would do these things, we have done them and we enter fiscal '27 in a stronger strategic position than at any point in our history.
Not a penny has moved from UltraTech balance sheet for any other purposes.

adds.what: 37 Mt further phased capacity additions committed, taking UltraTech India to 242.5 Mt by FY28
INR1,800 crore cable and wire capacity (INR800 crore spent)

growth.why: Management targets double-digit FY27 volume growth and 7-8% sustainable volume growth, backed by 37 Mt of phased capacity committed to reach 242.5 Mt by FY28 and ~90% utilisation, though no FY27 volume number is tied to specific commissioning dates.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: India Cements EBITDA rose from INR305/t (Q3) to INR497/t (Q4) and the efficiency programme is at INR185/t against a INR300/t target by FY28, but West Asia cost inflation (about INR90 crore bag hit in March, FX loss of INR120-130 crore) and unfactored diesel and fuel pressure cap near-term upside.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: phased, 37 Mt by FY28 (Q4 FY28 end-point)
rows.why: 37 Mt of further phased additions are committed, taking UltraTech India from about 200 Mt to 242.5 Mt by FY28, with utilisation at 90%; cable and wire INR1,800 crore (INR800 crore spent) launches around Q3 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets double-digit FY27 volume growth against 6.5% industry growth in FY26, backed by 90% utilisation and 37 Mt of phased capacity additions.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at about 90% across the network with 37 Mt already committed, and management plans INR8,000-10,000 crore of annual capex from internal accruals, so further expansion beyond 240 Mt is being planned.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management targets double-digit FY27 volume growth and 7-8% sustainable growth, and the April price hikes are described as sufficient to offset bag costs, but no revenue or margin guidance was raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: West Asia pressure is not yet fully in the numbers: diesel and June-quarter fuel (about INR1.77-1.8/kcal) are not factored in, bag costs rose from about INR9 to INR15 a bag in March, and the INR120-130 crore forex MTM hit is in EBITDA, though April price hikes are said to offset it.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: The INR1,800 crore cable and wire business has INR800 crore spent, with launch guided around the first month of Q3 FY27.

rows.label: Efficiency programme to INR300/t+ by FY28
rows.why: About INR185/t already delivered against a target above INR300/t, now expected to be exceeded by FY28.

rows.label: Leverage below 1x while funding capex
rows.why: Net debt/EBITDA is 0.94x consolidated and capex of INR8,000-10,000 crore a year is funded from internal accruals, with leverage guided to stay below 1x.

rows.label: April 2026 price hikes hold
rows.why: Price hikes taken in April are seen as offsetting bag costs of about INR6/bag, but grey cement prices rose only about 2.5% in Q4 and the monsoon is a test.

tone.note: Management was confident on capacity, volume growth and the dividend, but guarded on West Asia cost trajectory, diesel, forward pricing and the India Cements merger timeline; analysts pushed on those cost and integration points.
